belief: “I can’t trust anyone. If I let my guard down, I’ll be hurt again.”
belief_plain: I can’t trust anyone. If I let my guard down, I’ll be hurt again
origins: Trust breaks when someone who should have been safe was not. After that, keeping everyone out can feel like the only wisdom left. The lie stretches a real betrayal into a rule about every person, and often about God too. Caution with unsafe people is not the same thing as “I can’t trust anyone.” A counselor can help you sort who is unsafe from who might be safe, without rushing you. A counselor can help you work with this at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do it alone, or all at once.
self: If I let anyone close, I will be hurt again.
I can only count on myself.
God let it happen, so He is not safe either.
Needing people is how I got hurt.
I would rather be alone than risk it.
replacement: I was hurt, and that does not mean I can never trust anyone. I can trust God, and I can test trust slowly with safe people.
